identity.resolvedIdentity: The three-chamber lock complex at Ørje, opened in 1860 as part of the Halden Canal, distinct from the adjacent canal museum, former Ørje Brug, swing bridge, power station and the full waterway.
identity.identityProblem: The record combines one physical lock complex with the much longer Halden Canal and several adjacent technical and museum objects. The canonical coordinate must follow the locks without claiming the geometry of the entire canal environment.
identity.splitReason: The three lock chambers form one coherent destination. The museum, bridge and power station remain separately identifiable neighbouring objects.

explicit separation from museum, bridge and power station

evidence.finding: The municipality identifies the hand-operated locks west of Ørje centre, opened in 1860, with an aggregate lift of approximately ten metres.
evidence.reason: Confirms identity, operation and physical role.

evidence.finding: The municipality documents canal construction from 1852 to 1860 and distinguishes the Ørje and Strømsfoss lock installations from the full waterway.
evidence.reason: Defines the larger system and prevents overclaiming from the Ørje point.

evidence.finding: NVE documents the 1860 opening of Ørje locks, their role in timber transport and the continuation of floating until 1982.
evidence.reason: Confirms the technical and economic interpretation.

evidence.finding: The destination description identifies three lock chambers and a normal passage time of approximately 30 minutes.
evidence.reason: Confirms the chamber count and current operation.

evidence.finding: The museum is located in the former Ørje Brug pulp mill beside the locks and interprets canal, floating and steamboat history.
evidence.reason: Confirms an important neighbouring component while distinguishing it from the lock-complex coordinate.
